findings.failure_path: Each distinct valid line range adds both its encoded rows and its joined stream to spans for the duration of replay. The insertion happens before size, offset, or body validation. Many short results claiming different overlapping ranges can therefore retain many copies of a large skill, even when every result is rejected. The bridge can exhaust memory or miss the hook deadline while holding the conversation lock.
findings.smallest_fix: Cache one canonical stream and row offsets per skill. Validate each range against a view of that stream. Add a regression with distinct overlapping ranges that asserts retained canonical storage stays proportional to the skill size.

findings.failure_path: On a second write for the same key, the bridge skips checked_shadow and returns the original pathname. If the first handler replaced that name, the bridge writes the old inode and gives the next hook a path to the replacement. If the inode gained a hardlink, the bridge writes transcript content through a now multiply linked file. The new rename test stops before either reuse case.
findings.smallest_fix: Before a cached rewrite, verify that the held descriptor still satisfies the shadow checks and that the no-follow pathname identifies the same device and inode. Fail closed on mismatch and retain the original descriptor for cleanup. Extend the rename test through a second write.

findings.failure_path: When cleanup runs without a registered descriptor, it opens the current pathname and truncates any owned, singly linked regular file there. That can erase a replacement after setup failed before descriptor registration. The packet omits the cleanup callers, so it cannot establish that this branch is unreachable on an error exit.
findings.smallest_fix: Return when the event has no registered descriptor. Leave interrupted-event recovery to the stale sweep. Add a cleanup test that places a sentinel at the pathname with no descriptor registered and verifies its contents survive.

findings.failure_path: The release record marks the verifier finding fixed, but the frozen packet contains no current-candidate result for make test or the npm suite named in the completion standard. The attached challenge identifies the predecessor commit, and the focused test counts differ across the supplied records. A maintainer cannot determine which required checks passed on this delta.
findings.smallest_fix: Record the reviewed revision, commands, and actual outcomes for the focused, full repository, and package suites. Identify which revision produced each focused count and mark any outstanding check pending.

concern_results.conclusion: The quoted P1 is fixed for an event that populated a shadow. Cleanup truncates the retained descriptor, and the new Stop test checks both the renamed inode and the replacement file. A later write in the same event can still use an inode that no longer matches the path handed to hooks.
Descriptor reuse skips the ownership, link-count, and pathname checks on subsequent writes. Cleanup also retains a pathname-based truncation branch for events with no registered descriptor.

The sweep now takes the conversation lock before removing a legacy temp and catches directory iteration errors. Partial read replay introduces a separate memory failure path by retaining overlapping copies of canonical text for distinct ranges.

The rename test would catch the original cleanup defect. It ends after replacement, so it does not exercise another write through the cached descriptor. The two-skill assertion checks cache isolation. No supplied case bounds cache growth across distinct ranges. This was a static review.

The delta adds no operator flag, permission requirement, or migration step. The per-range cache adds a resource cost to replay of existing transcripts that can exceed the size of the transcript itself.

Legacy writers that use the same run lock are protected during temp cleanup. Reverting this delta alone restores pathname-based event cleanup and the quoted data-loss defect. Returning to the older replace-and-unlink implementation also restores checkpoint re-arming.

Sweep errors remain local to housekeeping. For release diagnosis, the validation record points to Local Verification, but the packet supplies no current-candidate outcomes there for the full repository and package suites.

The profile reports 48 bridge tests and the validation diff reports 53. The packet does not bind those runs to their respective revisions. The host observations support the sampled chunk formats. They establish neither a replay memory bound nor rejection of a canonical result paired with the wrong requested ByteOffset.

The descriptor binds cleanup to the populated inode. Policy hooks still receive a pathname, and a cached rewrite can succeed after that pathname has changed. Partial read headers also control how much canonical text the bridge retains before it verifies the body.

Neither quoted contract is modified. The root contract requires current-candidate verification for hook behavior changes. The focused test count and predecessor challenge are visible, but the required full-lane result is missing from the supplied release evidence.
